skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=False, severity=minor. Keep the price claim: price swung from 0.0 to -3.1 pts, about $2.75B of 2025 revenue, the worst in six years of 10-K tables (perimeter differs before 2023). Drop or soften 'rebate accruals outran sales for two years'. skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=True, severity=major. Conceded: The drag is explained: STELARA biosimilars plus Part D redesign, named in the 10-K (p.28, p.37) and in prepared remarks on both 2025 calls. skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=True, severity=major. Only a narrower claim would be non-obvious: price erosion outside STELARA that continues into 2026 after Part D redesign has lapped. skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=True, severity=major. Conceded: The price leg is material and correctly computed. The rebate-versus-sales gap is mostly a base error (worldwide versus U.S. sales). Narrowed: A finding would need price erosion outside STELARA to continue into 2026, and the 10-Qs have no price/volume split to show it.

verdict_reason: Killed as said by management. Both skeptics confirm the numbers (JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.28, printed p.23: price -3.1, STELARA decline about 6.2 points of growth on the same page) and both accept the -3.1 pts / ~$2.75B / six-year ranking. Materiality flipped from held to refuted in round 2 after re-reading p.28, p.37 (Part D redesign in segment margin bullets) and the 2025Q3 p.6 and 2025Q4 p.6 calls, where STELARA's decline is attributed to 'biosimilar competition and Part D redesign'. Obviousness also showed the rebate-vs-sales leg is a base error: against U.S. IM sales (+7.0%, 10-K FY2025 p.29) the 2025 gap is 0.6 pts, and AbbVie's provisions also outgrew revenue. No remaining disagreement. The only non-obvious version (non-STELARA price erosion continuing into 2026) cannot be built: the 10-Qs carry no price/volume split. Confirmed refuted, not merely unrefuted.

skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=False, severity=major. Narrow to: the IM plant count moved from 4 U.S./14 non-U.S. to 3/16 in one year (same Item 2 paragraph), while IM square footage grew and the location of Puerto Rico plants is undisclosed. The generic MFN zero rate ends January 20, 2029, but J&J's own agreement term is confidential. The $0.9-1.2B figure is an illustration at a 15% rate on a plant-count share, not a bound.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=False, severity=major. Conceded: It is the least obvious item in the file. The IM split, the plant exits and the 2029 date are unsaid, and management's 'more U.S. facilities than any other country' counts all segments, which makes the IM split worth showing. Held: The exposure base, rate and end date are all assumptions. The 2029 date may not bind J&J (Annex II, confidential terms), and the plant-count shift has no P&L size. Narrowed: Material only as a conditional risk of $0.29-0.54 EPS a year at 15-20%. Range widened from round 1 to include the 20% rate. Not a forecast, not a bound.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=False, severity=minor. Frame it as a timing race. The Innovative Medicine footprint moved offshore in 2025 while management's onshoring promise finishes 'through early 2029', the same quarter the zero tariff ends. skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=False, severity=minor. Conceded: J&J's 2029 end date is not proven. Applying 15% to every non-U.S. plant is wrong, since non-EU origin pays 20%, rising to 100%. Plant count is not production value. '$0.9-1.2B bound' should be called an illustration. Held: The plant drift is unsaid and like-for-like, and the floor-space table on the same page tilts offshore too. It survives the obviousness test as the least obvious JNJ item. verdict_reason: J&J's drug-plant footprint moved offshore in 2025 on a like-for-like Item 2 paragraph (U.S. Innovative Medicine plants 4 to 3, non-U.S. 14 to 16; company-wide floor space Europe +11.4% and Western Hemisphere ex-U.S. +17.4% vs U.S. +5.0%, U.S. share 30.1% to 29.3%), and this was never discussed on any 2025Q4-2026Q3 call. The generic Section 232 zero rate for MFN signers ends January 20, 2029, after which J&J's patented drug imports would pay 15% (EU/Swiss origin) or 20% (rising to 100% on April 2, 2030). Only if J&J's confidential exemption ends at that generic sunset and its $55B U.S. build-out (two new plants announced, 'through early 2029') does not yet cover U.S. demand, the illustrative cost is about $0.9-1.6B pre-tax, $0.29-0.54 EPS a year (about 3-5% of the $11.10 2026 guide). This is a conditional risk, not a forecast or a bound. | Narrowed; both skeptics hold it (materiality refuted=false major, obviousness refuted=false minor) after narrowing. I verified the source myself: JNJ:10k_FY2025.md page 23 (printed p.18) reads 'three facilities are used by the Innovative Medicine segment ... Outside of the U.S., 16 facilities', IM square feet 5,245k, U.S. 22 facilities/3,037k, Europe 22/5,035k, W. Hemisphere ex-U.S. 7/1,054k, total 63/10,363k; JNJ:10k_FY2024.md page 23 (printed p.18) reads 'four facilities ... 14 facilities', IM 4,696k, U.S. 23/2,892k, Europe 21/4,521k, W. Hemisphere ex-U.S. 7/898k, total 64/9,607k. verify_quote passes on both sentences. Arithmetic: Europe 5,035/4,521 = +11.4%, U.S. 3,037/2,892 = +5.0%, U.S. share 30.1% to 29.3%. Caveats I add: the geographic floor-space table is company-wide, not IM-only, and IM floor space grew 11.7%, so the floor-space tilt supports but does not prove an IM shift; the Q2 2026 restructuring (JNJ:10q_2026Q2.md p.48, $650-750M, 'exit certain manufacturing locations', complete by end of 2029) names no locations, so it is not evidence of direction and I drop it from the drift claim. I read Proclamation 11020 (policy_gov ... section232_pharma.md p.1): clause (3)(e) zero rate 'until January 20, 2029' but 'shall also apply per the terms of the agreements listed in Annex II'; (3)(b) 20% rising to 100% on April 2, 2030; (3)(c) 15% for EU/Japan/Korea/Swiss origin. J&J's press release (2026-01-08 p.1) footnotes 'Specific terms of the agreement remain confidential.' Conceded by both: J&J's own end date is unproven, plant count is not import value, 15%-everywhere is wrong, and the dollar figure is an illustration. Materiality ruling: I read the conditional form as clearing the case's materiality test, narrowly. The scenario value ($0.29-0.54 EPS, 3-5% of guided EPS, recurring from 2029 and stepping up in 2030) is well above the 'few cents of EPS' rule of thumb, and an investor deciding on a multi-year hold would change their view of the 2029-2030 earnings path if the exemption is not extended. It does not clear as a high-materiality finding because both triggers are undisclosed and cannot be probability-weighted from the index, and the hard fact (one plant each way) has no P&L size by itself. Obviousness: confirmed low; both skeptics checked the calls and tariff talk is MedTech-only, and management's 'more manufacturing facilities in the United States than in any other country' (2025Q3 p.9) counts all segments, which is why the IM split is worth showing. Facts confirmed; the dollar risk is unrefuted but conditional.

Confirmed as a fact, J&J-specific; it does not clear the case's materiality test on its own because no P&L impact can be shown, so it counts as a narrowed row, not a material finding.

skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=True, severity=fatal. The wording change is real (10q_2025Q2 p.50 says 'Medicare Part D redesign'; 10q_2026Q2 p.40 says 'unfavorable patient mix and inventory dynamics'), but the inference fails on period logic. Part D redesign took effect January 2025, so 2026 year-over-year comparisons lap a 2025 base that already includes it. Dropping it as a growth driver in 2026 text is expected, not a relabel. The growth figure is cherry-picked: U.S. ERLEADA was +4.7% in Q2 but +10.2% for H1 (738 vs 670, 10-Q p.26), and the 2026Q3 call gives ERLEADA +9.4% (p.6). The 10-Q sentence the reader quotes also names 'inventory dynamics', which the math ignores. The 8.2-point gap sets U.S. growth against international reported growth, which includes FX. It then applies a one-quarter gap to a full-year base. The result, $119M, is about 0.13% of revenue, below any materiality threshold.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=True, severity=major. Conceded: It is unsaid, and the XARELTO case is a fair test of whether 'patient mix' still means Medicare channel. Held: It is immaterial and the period logic (lapping) explains most of it. Narrowed: From fatal to major: wording drift only. The XARELTO thread is open but unsized.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=False, severity=minor. Keep it as a disclosure-drift observation, with the lapping explanation addressed head-on. It is non-obvious only if 'patient mix' is still a Medicare-channel effect after the lap, for example XARELTO still citing 'favorable patient mix' in 2026, as it did with Part D in 2025.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=True, severity=fatal. Conceded: Fatal, as materiality argued: the lapping logic plus the cherry-picked quarter. Held: Nothing. Being unsaid is not enough when the innocent reading fits. Narrowed: Withdrawn.

verdict_reason: Killed as immaterial and explained by lapping. Obviousness moved to fatal in round 2: U.S. ERLEADA was +4.7% in Q2 but +10.2% for H1 (JNJ:10q_2026Q2.md p.26) and +9.4% on the 2026Q3 call (p.6), the 10-Q sentence also cites 'inventory dynamics', and the wording change is what lapping a January 2025 Part D change predicts. Materiality: $119M is about 0.13% of revenue. The XARELTO 'favorable patient mix' thread (10-Q p.40, 10-K p.31) is open but unsized. Confirmed refuted.
